title: Stepped shaft in tension, D/d = 2, r/d = 0.2 (3D solid)
description:
Stepped round bar (shaft) with a shoulder fillet, in axial tension. 3D solid.
Geometry file (STEP): the full 3D bar; its axis is the z axis, the small end face lies in the plane z = 0.
Purpose: a turned steel tension rod whose diameter steps from d = 20 mm to D = 40 mm. The step is blended by a fillet of radius r = 4 mm, tangent to the small cylinder and to the flat annular shoulder face in the plane z = 60 mm. The small-diameter section runs from the end face at z = 0 to the shoulder; the large-diameter section runs from the shoulder plane to the end face at z = 120 mm.
Material: steel, linear elastic and isotropic, E = 200 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.3.
Load: a total axial tensile force P = 31.416 kN, applied as a uniform axial traction (pulling outward) on the large end face z = 120 mm. The nominal stress on the small diameter, 4P/(pi d^2), is 100 MPa.
Analysis: linear static, small displacements.
Supports: the small end face z = 0 is supported axially only (zero axial displacement, free to move in its plane: a frictionless support). Add only the minimum extra constraints needed to remove the remaining rigid-body motions (in-plane translation, rotation about the axis) without stressing the part. Exploiting symmetry is allowed.
Report:
  peak_stress_fillet: the maximum value of the maximum principal stress s1 on the fillet surface [Pa];
  elongation: the average axial displacement uz of the large end face (z = 120 mm) [m].
